title: Score CART (Cardiac Arrest Risk Triage) — triage du risque d'arrêt cardiaque

how_to_use.why:
- Predicting deterioration in ward patients may be difficult. Validated risk scores such as CART may help.
- Outperformed [MEWS](nabda:calc.modified-early-warning-score-mews-clinical-deterioration) at predicting cardiac arrest in one study (AUROC 0.84 vs 0.78) ([Churpek 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3673668/)).
how_to_use.pearls:
- A systematic review of early warning system (EWS) scores, including CART, concluded that such scores perform well to predict cardiac arrest but that impact on outcomes and resource utilization is still uncertain, and current evidence is insufficient ([Smith 2014](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25296111)).
- Requires accurate respiratory rate.

next_steps.advice: Les patients avec un score CART élevé peuvent bénéficier d’une intensification des soins. Utiliser le jugement clinique en plus des scores de stratification du risque pour prendre des décisions relatives à l’orientation.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| CART Score | Risk of cardiac arrest within 48 hours |
| --- | --- |
| ≤20 | Low |
| >20 | High* |

*In the original study ([Churpek 2012](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3378796/)), scores >20 were 91.9% specific for predicting cardiac arrest within 48 hours, and 90% specific in a validation cohort ([Churpek 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3673668/)).
medium_description: Predicts risque de dans-hôpital cardiac arrest.
